newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: DRB boss says fundamentals strong - paper.
newsitem.headline: DRB boss says fundamentals strong - paper.

text.p: The new chief of Malaysian auto and industrial group headed by Diversified Resources Bhd (DRB) said the fundamentals of the group had not changed with the death of its former chairman.

"As much as we have suffered from the loss of Tan Sri (Yahaya Ahmad), the fundamentals of the company are strong, and will continue to be strong," new group chairman Saleh Sulong said in an interview with Malaysian business weekly, The Edge, published on Monday.

Former group chairman Yahaya was killed in a helicopter crash last Monday night, prompting the company to suspend the shares of nine companies controlled by him. The shares will be requoted at the opening of trade on Monday March 10.
The DRB-Hicom group controls national carmaker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton).
"Why should they sell (shares upon requotation)?," said Saleh when asked what his advice to investors was.
"Whatever projects that we have will be pursued with the same vigour and pace," he added.
